title: Courtesy Late-Charge Rates for Microsoft 365 Subscriptions with a Clean Payment Record
content:
**Rate clause.** On a Microsoft 365 Cloud Subscriptions (CSP) annual cycle invoice, the monthly late-charge rate follows the subscription's own late-charge record:

- no late charge posted on the subscription less than twelve whole months before the assessment date, and the subscription has renewed at least twice: the rate is **1.0 percent** of the past-due balance;
- no late charge posted in that period, and the subscription has renewed fewer than twice: the rate is **1.25 percent**;
- otherwise, no courtesy rate applies.

**The twelve-month look-back.** A late charge posted on the same day of the month twelve months earlier is not less than twelve whole months before, so it does not count. Only late charges posted on this subscription's billing ledger count.

## Decision table

| Late charge on the subscription less than twelve whole months before assessment | Renewals of the subscription | Monthly rate |
|---|---|---|
| none | 2 or more | 1.0 percent |
| none | 0 or 1 | 1.25 percent |
| one or more | any | no courtesy rate |

## Look-back boundary (hypothetical dates, assessment on 1 September)

| Latest earlier late charge posted on | Counts? |
|---|---|
| 1 September of the previous year | No. It is exactly twelve months earlier. |
| 1 October of the previous year | Yes. It falls less than twelve whole months before. |

## Hypothetical illustration

A subscription has renewed three times, and its last late charge was posted on 1 September of the previous year. Assessed on 1 September, it takes 1.0 percent, so a past-due balance of 6000.00 USD gives 60.00. If its last late charge had been posted on 1 October of the previous year, no courtesy rate would apply.
